 How to apply for heating aid as Philadelphia weather gets colder 
 Kylan Watson

 As colder temperatures settle across the Philadelphia region and winter approaches, thousands of low-income households are being urged to apply for heating assistance before energy bills climb even higher.
 Applications are now open for the federally funded Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, known as LIHEAP, which can provide eligible residents with grants to help keep their homes warm and prevent utility shutoffs.
 With utility costs continuing to strain household budgets, advocates and energy providers say LIHEAP remains one of the most important resources available to families struggling to pay their heating bills.
 The program provides grants paid directly to utility companies and can help cover energy costs, prevent service terminations and address certain home energy-related needs. Applications are being accepted through April 23, 2027.
 LIHEAP is available to qualifying low-income households statewide. In Pennsylvania, income eligibility ranges from $23,940 for a one-person household to $49,500 for a family of four.
 Applicants must provide documentation that may include pay stubs, Social Security award letters, pension or retirement statements, the names and birth dates of household members and Social Security numbers.
 “We encourage customers to apply while funding is still available," said Patricia King, manager at PECO. “How it helps is with their heating bills. Everyone needs a little bit of assistance, especially our lower-income customers.”
 King said between 40,000 and 45,000 PECO customers receive LIHEAP grants annually, but many more residents likely qualify.
 “Approximately 40,000 to 45,000 customers benefit from LIHEAP grants at PECO,” King said. “But we would like to see that number go up. We know more customers are eligible, so we're always trying to get the word out to make sure more customers benefit from the program.”
 Beyond LIHEAP, PECO offers year-round assistance programs, including its Customer Assistance Program, or CAP, which allows participants to pay a percentage of their income for monthly utility bills instead of standard rates.
 The company also provides hardship grants and energy-efficiency programs.
 “Reach out to us. Nine times out of 10 there is something that we can offer you to bring some assistance to your household,” King said.
 To help residents learn more about available aid, PECO will host an Energy Assistance Day from 2 p.m. to 6 p.m. Nov. 5 at its headquarters, 2301 Market St.
 Philadelphia Gas Works, meanwhile, said approximately 70,000 of its customers received LIHEAP grants last year but noted that far more city residents remain eligible for assistance.
 “In Philadelphia, approximately 70,000 grants were received by PGW customers,” a PGW representative said in a statement. “PGW has been engaging in significant customer outreach in the hopes of encouraging an increase in Philadelphia LIHEAP applications this year.
 "Given that there are roughly 190,000 eligible families in Philadelphia for LIHEAP, it is essential that all eligible households take advantage of this opportunity to obtain this up to $1,000 in heating assistance that does not need to be repaid," they added.
 PGW officials said the utility also offers hardship grants and payment assistance which provides financial help for customers experiencing hardships such as medical emergencies, unemployment or other temporary crises.
 The utility said roughly 104,000 customers qualify for both LIHEAP and its Customer Responsibility Program, or CRP, an income-based payment plan that also offers debt forgiveness.
 PGW will host a free LIHEAP Day event from 2 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. Nov. 19 at Center in the Park, 5818 Germantown Ave. Residents also may schedule appointments through PGW's Neighborhood Energy Centers, text "CASH" to 77037 to receive an application or download an application online.
 “Roughly 104,000 PGW customers are eligible for both LIHEAP and PGW’s Customer Responsibility Program, an affordable bill discount program that helps low-income customers by providing a monthly bill that is based on household income and that also provides debt forgiveness,” PGW said in a statement. “It is easy to apply, and customers can sign up on a smart phone, by mail or by fax. A customer on CRP may have a monthly payment as low as $25.”
 Updated at 9:27 a.m. on 11/5/2026 to clarify how payment assistance is provided.
